title: React Web Development
description: Beginner-to-advanced React reference covering component design, JSX, state, events, forms, Hooks, effects, context, reducers, Suspense, errors, performance, accessibility, and testing.

sections.title: Components, JSX & Rendering
sections.description: Build pure component trees from immutable inputs.

subtopics.title: Function Components, Props & JSX
subtopics.description: Components are functions React calls. Props are immutable snapshots; JSX describes UI and embeds expressions with braces.

callouts.title: Never Call Components Directly
callouts.text: Render <Avatar /> rather than Avatar(). React must control component and Hook invocation to preserve identity and scheduling.

callouts.title: Keep Rendering Pure
callouts.text: Given the same props, state, and context, rendering should produce the same result without mutating external values or starting side effects.

subtopics.title: Conditional Rendering, Lists & Keys
subtopics.description: Use normal JavaScript control flow. Keys identify siblings across insertion, deletion, and reordering.

callouts.title: Keys Are Identity, Not Warnings
callouts.text: Use stable domain IDs. Index and random keys can transfer local state to the wrong item or remount every child; key is not passed as a prop.

subtopics.title: Composition, children & Slots
subtopics.description: Compose specialized UI from smaller parts. Pass elements as children or named slots instead of building inheritance hierarchies.

callouts.title: Prefer Narrow APIs
callouts.text: Expose semantic props and slots that preserve component invariants. Avoid a large matrix of boolean appearance props or leaking internal DOM structure.

sections.title: State, Events & Forms
sections.description: Model state minimally and update it without mutation.

subtopics.title: useState, Snapshots & Functional Updates
subtopics.description: State belongs to a component position. Setting state queues a future render; current handlers retain the snapshot from the render that created them.

callouts.title: Do Not Mutate State
callouts.text: Mutating objects or arrays can leave React unaware of changes and corrupt previous snapshots. Create a new container and new changed values.

subtopics.title: Minimal State, Derivation & Reset
subtopics.description: Store the minimum source of truth; derive filtered, formatted, and aggregate values during rendering. Change a key to intentionally reset a subtree.

callouts.title: Avoid Synchronized Copies
callouts.text: Do not mirror props or derived data into state with an Effect. It adds an extra render and creates stale synchronization bugs.

subtopics.title: Events & Controlled Forms
subtopics.description: Event handlers perform user-triggered work. Controlled fields receive value/checked plus a change handler from state.

callouts.title: Use Semantic HTML First
callouts.text: A form and submit button provide keyboard, accessibility, and browser behavior. Avoid clickable divs and custom controls when native elements fit.

sections.title: Hooks, Effects & Refs
sections.description: Reuse stateful logic and synchronize only with systems outside React.

subtopics.title: Rules of Hooks & Custom Hooks
subtopics.description: Call Hooks only at the top level of React components or custom Hooks. Custom Hooks share logic, not state instances.

callouts.title: Hooks Must Be Unconditional
callouts.text: Do not call Hooks in conditions, loops, callbacks, or after conditional returns. React relies on identical call order to associate Hook state.

subtopics.title: useEffect & Cleanup
subtopics.description: Effects synchronize a component with external systems after commit. Dependencies must include every reactive value read by the effect.

callouts.title: Effects Are Escape Hatches
callouts.text: If work can happen during render or in an event handler, it probably does not need an Effect. Framework data APIs are usually better for route data than manual fetch Effects.

callouts.title: Strict Mode Probes Cleanup
callouts.text: Development may run setup, cleanup, then setup again to reveal missing cleanup. Fix the effect rather than suppressing the probe.

subtopics.title: useRef, DOM Refs & Imperative Handles
subtopics.description: Refs hold values not required for rendering and point to DOM nodes. Updating current does not re-render.

callouts.title: State Is for Rendered Data
callouts.text: If a value affects output, store it in state. Reading/writing refs during rendering breaks purity except predictable one-time initialization.

sections.title: Shared & Complex State
sections.description: Lift state to its owner and scale transitions explicitly.

subtopics.title: Lifting State & Context
subtopics.description: Lift state to the closest common owner. Context broadcasts values through a subtree and suits stable cross-cutting data such as theme or authenticated identity.

callouts.title: Context Is Not Automatic State Architecture
callouts.text: Frequently changing broad context re-renders consumers and hides dependencies. Split contexts, colocate state, or use a specialized external store when necessary.

subtopics.title: useReducer & Transition Design
subtopics.description: Reducers centralize complex state transitions as pure functions. Actions describe events; reducers calculate next state without effects.

callouts.title: Reducer Must Be Pure
callouts.text: Do not fetch, log, mutate, generate nondeterministic IDs, or write storage in a reducer. Trigger effects around dispatch or in framework/business layers.

subtopics.title: External Stores & useSyncExternalStore
subtopics.description: Use useSyncExternalStore to subscribe React safely to state owned outside React, with a stable snapshot and optional server snapshot.

callouts.title: Snapshot Identity Matters
callouts.text: getSnapshot must return the same immutable value while the store is unchanged. Returning a new object each call can cause infinite re-rendering.

sections.title: Async UI, Actions, Suspense & Errors
sections.description: Represent pending work and failure at explicit boundaries.

subtopics.title: useTransition & useDeferredValue
subtopics.description: Transitions mark non-urgent updates so urgent input stays responsive. Deferred values let a slow subtree lag behind a rapidly changing value.

callouts.title: Transitions Do Not Make Work Faster
callouts.text: They change scheduling priority and interruption behavior. Optimize expensive computation, data access, and bundle size separately.

subtopics.title: Suspense & use
subtopics.description: Suspense shows a fallback while supported children suspend. The use API reads a Promise or context and integrates with Suspense/error boundaries.

callouts.title: Use Framework Data Integration
callouts.text: Suspense data contracts are best supplied by a framework or compatible cache. Creating a new Promise during every render causes repeated suspension.

subtopics.title: Actions, Optimistic State & Error Boundaries
subtopics.description: useActionState coordinates action result/pending state; useOptimistic shows immediate feedback. Error boundaries catch rendering failures below them, not event-handler errors.

callouts.title: Optimism Needs Reconciliation
callouts.text: Design pending identity, duplicate submission, server normalization, rejection, and rollback. Never imply irreversible success before the server commits it.

sections.title: Performance, Accessibility & Testing
sections.description: Measure before memoizing and test behavior through the user-visible surface.

subtopics.title: memo, useMemo & useCallback
subtopics.description: Memoization is a performance optimization. Use it when measured work or referential equality is important, not to make incorrect code function.

callouts.title: Memoization Has Cost
callouts.text: Dependency comparison, retained values, and complexity can cost more than recomputation. Profile production builds and first fix state placement, effects, and expensive rendering.

subtopics.title: React Compiler, Activity & Effect Events
subtopics.description: React Compiler 1.0 can automatically memoize eligible components and Hooks. React 19.2 adds Activity for hiding/restoring UI state and useEffectEvent for non-reactive logic invoked from effects.

callouts.title: Adopt Compiler Incrementally
callouts.text: Keep components pure, run the compiler lint rules, measure output, and remove manual memoization only when the compiler and profiler show it is redundant. Effect Events are called from effects and are not a way to suppress real dependencies.

subtopics.title: Accessibility & Safe DOM Output
subtopics.description: Use semantic elements, labels, headings, focus management, keyboard behavior, and announced status/errors. React escapes text values by default.

callouts.title: Raw HTML Is a Trust Boundary
callouts.text: dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses escaping. Sanitize untrusted HTML with a maintained policy and prefer structured rendering.

subtopics.title: Testing & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Test output and interaction rather than component internals; preserve strict-mode compatibility and cleanup.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Components and Hooks remain pure
□ Props/state are never mutated
□ List keys use stable domain identity
□ State is minimal and owned at the correct level
□ Effects only synchronize external systems and clean up
□ Hook dependencies are complete
□ Loading, empty, error, retry, and optimistic rollback exist
□ Semantic HTML, labels, focus, and keyboard behavior work
□ User interactions are tested by role/name
□ Memoization follows measurement
□ Client bundle and re-render hotspots are profiled
□ Raw HTML and external URLs cross explicit security boundaries

callouts.title: Test Like a User
callouts.text: Query by role, label, and visible name; perform real events; assert rendered results. Avoid testing Hook call order, private state, or implementation-only selectors.
